title: Codex CLI: Everything You Need in 12 mins
summary: Twelve-minute Codex CLI tour: exec mode, plan mode, slash commands, permissions flags, skills and Playwright testing.

assertions.quote: in plan mode, Codex will start asking questions to iron out the details

verdicts.note: Requirements clarification before implementation is well-established practice and widely reported to reduce agent rework.

assertions.quote: context files tend to reduce task success rates compared to providing no repository context while also increasing inference cost by over 20%

verdicts.note: A 2026 study found LLM-generated context files slightly hurt success and raised cost, while concise human-written ones helped a little; the effect depends on content and length.

assertions.quote: /init is another command that you probably should not use ... this file pollutes Codex context more than it actually helps

verdicts.note: Persistent instruction files measurably steer agent behavior; overlong or contradictory ones reduce adherence.

assertions.quote: Codex opens the browser by itself and starts testing the application

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: Codex came back with actionable items, and also sorted by priorities

verdicts.note: AI reviewers do catch real defects missed by humans, though with notable false-positive rates; complement, not replacement.
